estimated_study_time.text: Plan for about 2 hours of study for this chapter.

chapter_summary.text: This lesson provides practice for Listening: Multiple-choice, choose single answer and Listening: Multiple-choice, choose multiple answers. It focuses on listening skills such as gist, detailed information, speaker purpose, organization, inference and stylistics, and asks learners to analyze item format, rubrics, strategies, timed practice items and feedback.

evidence_spans.quote: This lesson provides skills practice for the PTE Academic item types Listening: Multiple-choice, choose single answer and Listening: Multiple-choice, choose multiple answers.

Detailed information: Listen for and identify specific details, facts, opinions, definitions or sequences of events

Organization: Listen for and identify the overall organization and connections between pieces of information
Inference: Listen for information that helps you infer meanings, form generalizations, make predictions, find relationships or draw conclusions
Stylistics: Listen for and identify the speaker’s attitude, feelings or degree of certainty on an issue

core_lessons.title: Read The Prompt For The Listening Skill

explanation.text: For these listening multiple-choice items, read the prompt carefully so you know what information to listen for, which listening skill is being tested, and which listening strategy to apply.

evidence_spans.quote: they must always read the prompt carefully to make sure they know exactly what type of information they are being asked to listen for
which type of listening skill is being tested) and which type of listening strategy they should apply.

core_lessons.title: Use The Preparation Time On The Prompt

explanation.text: For this item type, there are 7 seconds to prepare before listening; this is enough time to read and consider the prompt, but generally not enough time to read the options as well.

evidence_spans.quote: for this item type, they have 7 seconds to prepare before listening.
This is enough time to read and consider the item prompt, but is in general not enough time to read the options as well

explanation.text: When listening, take notes using key words or abbreviations only, and keep the notes brief and relevant.

evidence_spans.quote: they should write key words or abbreviations only when taking notes.
they need to remain focused while listening and take brief but relevant notes.

core_lessons.title: Stay Focused If You Miss Something

explanation.text: If parts of a passage are unclear or not understood, remain focused and continue listening, because understanding every word is not always necessary and worrying about missed words can cause more information to be missed.

evidence_spans.quote: if there are parts of a passage that they do not hear clearly or do not understand they should remain focused and continue to listen.
It is not always necessary for them to understand or catch every word in the recording
worrying about misheard or misunderstood words will cause them to miss more information.

explanation.text: An important listening skill is quickly identifying information that is redundant or not relevant to the listening purpose, then dismissing it.

evidence_spans.quote: an important skill they need to develop when listening for particular information is how to quickly identify information that is redundant, or not relevant for, their listening purpose.
which they can therefore quickly dismiss.

explanation.text: For gist, listen for a topic sentence, key words explaining the main idea, or a concluding sentence. For detailed information, listen for key words explaining secondary or supporting ideas, such as where, when and how.

evidence_spans.quote: Listen for: topic sentence; key words that explain main idea; a concluding sentence, etc
Listen for: key words that explain secondary/supporting ideas, e.g. words that describe where, when, how, etc

worked_examples.title: A NOT Prompt In A Multiple-Answer Item

example.text: Prompt: Which options do NOT correctly match a material with its reason for use? Before listening, underline NOT and decide that you are listening for mismatches, not just true statements.

explanation.text: The practice item asks learners to select more than one response and asks which options do NOT correctly link materials and their rationale for use in skyscraper construction. The lesson explains that NOT makes the prompt difficult because learners are looking for false responses and must identify options with redundant or incorrect information.

evidence_spans.quote: Listen to the recording and answer the question by selecting the correct responses. You will need to select more than one response.
Which of the following do NOT correctly link materials and their rationale for use in the construction of skyscrapers?
‘NOT’ shows that they are looking for false responses, i.e. they have to be able to identify the options containing redundant or incorrect information and select these

example.text: If the prompt asks why glass walls are used, your notes might separate useful details from extra background: useful notes could include weatherproof, light in, lighter than masonry or concrete; extra background such as a historical date may not answer the prompt.

explanation.text: In the transcript activity, details about the properties of glass and steel are relevant, while the phrase “beginning after World War II” is redundant; the reasons why glass became popular should be noted.

evidence_spans.quote: Relevant Details about the properties of glass and steel should be noted
Although phrases such as ‘beginning after World War II’ are redundant, the reasons why glass became popular should be noted

example.text: When the instruction says only one response is correct, choose one option. When it says you need to select more than one response, check all options and select each correct one.

explanation.text: For choose single answer, the instruction is to select the correct response and only one response is correct. For choose multiple answers, the instruction is to select all the correct responses and more than one response is needed.

evidence_spans.quote: Listen to the recording and answer the question by selecting the correct  response. Only one response is correct.
Listen to the recording and answer the question by selecting all the correct responses. You will  need to select more than one response.

misconception.text: The 7-second preparation time should be used to read the prompt and all the answer options before the recording begins.

correction.text: The 7 seconds are enough to read and consider the item prompt, but generally not enough to read the options as well.

evidence_spans.quote: they have 7 seconds to prepare before listening. This is enough time to read and consider the item prompt, but is in general not enough time to read the options as well

misconception.text: If you miss or do not understand a word, you must stop and work it out before continuing.

correction.text: If parts of a passage are not heard clearly or not understood, remain focused and continue listening; it is not always necessary to understand every word.

evidence_spans.quote: if there are parts of a passage that they do not hear clearly or do not understand they should remain focused and continue to listen.
It is not always necessary for them to understand or catch every word in the recording

misconception.text: For listening multiple-choice items, changing your first answer is usually better than keeping it.

correction.text: For listening multiple-choice items, it is better to stick with first guesses rather than make changes to responses.

evidence_spans.quote: for listening multiple-choice items it is better to stick with their first guesses rather than to make changes to their responses.

question.text: In a listening multiple-choice prompt, what should you identify before the recording starts: the topic only, or the type of information you are being asked to listen for?

answer.text: Identify the type of information you are being asked to listen for, which listening skill is being tested, and which listening strategy you should apply.

question.text: A prompt says: “What is the lecture mainly about?” Which listening skill from this lesson is most directly being tested?
A prompt contains the word “NOT.” What should you be especially careful to select?

answer.text: Select the responses that contain incorrect or redundant information, rather than the responses that correctly match the recording.

question.text: During the 7-second preparation period, what is the safest priority?

answer.text: Read and consider the item prompt, then decide what to listen for.

question.text: When taking notes during the recording, should you try to write full sentences or brief key words and abbreviations?

answer.text: Use brief key words and abbreviations.

review_checklist.text: I can distinguish between choose single answer and choose multiple answers instructions.
I can read a prompt and decide whether it asks for gist, details, purpose, organization, inference or stylistics.
I can use the 7-second preparation time to focus on the prompt and decide what to listen for.
I can stay focused when I miss a word instead of letting one unclear part distract me.
I can take brief, relevant notes using key words or abbreviations.
I can identify redundant information and dismiss it when it does not answer the prompt.
